metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the presence of the adapter's 'N additional blocking findings omitted' sentinel line (adapter.py:136-139) forces REFUSE, since the visible `- (<crit>)` lines are then a strict subset and 'exactly {bugfix-size-attestation}' can never be safely concluded — add an AC covering a >10-finding block.
evidence: adapter.py:130 `for f in blocking[:10]:` caps rendered findings at 10

adapter.py:136-139 appends `f"{omitted} additional blocking {noun} omitted from this summary."` — this line does NOT match a `- (<criterion-id>)` shape, so a set derived purely from `- (…)` lines silently drops the omitted findings
Plan step 1 says to parse 'the `- (<criterion-id>) ...` lines' with no mention of the omitted-count sentinel
findings.finding: The step-2 'proceed only if that set is EXACTLY {bugfix-size-attestation}' decision rule does not account for the adapter's finding-list truncation: the bot vote message renders only the first 10 blocking findings as `- (<crit>)` lines and replaces the rest with a non-`- (…)` line 'N additional blocking findings omitted from this summary.' A block with >10 findings never presents its full criterion set to the parser.
findings.location: Design step 2 ('Proceed only if that set is EXACTLY {"bugfix-size-attestation"}'); AC line 'a block containing bugfix-size-attestation PLUS any other blocking finding is still REFUSED'
scenarios: A change accrues >10 blocking findings on the current revision where bugfix-size-attestation is among the first 10 rendered; the parser sees 10 finding lines plus an omitted-count sentinel and must decide the 'EXACTLY one' rule
findings.suggested_fix: In step 2, add: if the vote message contains the '…additional blocking finding(s) omitted…' sentinel, refuse unconditionally (the full blocking set is not observable). Add an AC that a block with >10 findings including bugfix-size-attestation is REFUSED.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the fallback for a failed criterion-id parse or a non-matching ticket-id extraction: REFUSE (fail-closed), and add a test asserting a truncated/unparseable bugfix-size finding message is refused rather than accepted or crashing.
evidence: Step 3 itself flags a truncation dependency: 'it appears before Gerrit's message truncation' — acknowledging the extraction can be defeated by truncation, yet stating no fallback
adapter.py:133 truncates the finding detail at 240 chars (`full_detail[:239]…`), and the plan relies on the ticket-id phrase landing inside that window; no branch is described for when it does not
The module's existing contract is fail-closed (retrigger.py:15-19), but the plan does not state that a failed parse/extraction must REFUSE
findings.finding: The plan specifies no fallback when the criterion-id line parse (steps 1-2) or the ticket-id phrase extraction (step 3, `but bug <id> has no acceptable plan-review attestation`) fails to match — e.g. message-shape drift or an unforeseen truncation. The failed-sub-step outcome is left unspecified despite the module being fail-closed.
scenarios: A future change to _teaching_finding wording, or an unusually long ticket id / reason pushing the 'but bug <id>' phrase past the 240-char truncation, leaves the ticket-id regex with no match at re-review time
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the 'What must still refuse' section: 'a bugfix-size-attestation block whose criterion-id set or named ticket id cannot be parsed from the bot's own vote message — refuse fail-closed.' Back it with a test that truncates the finding message before the ticket-id phrase.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State which ticket store the retrigger-side classify_plan_review_attestation reads and guarantee it reflects the just-pushed attestation and can resolve its storage anchor (e.g. force a fresh origin/tickets fetch/materialize before classifying, or pass an explicit repo_root of a synced snapshot), and add a test that the arm accepts when the attestation was pushed after the finding was cast.
evidence: The gate that produced the finding runs inside a per-review clone that freshly fetches origin/tickets (gerrit_client.py:381-410); the retrigger runs in the RECEIVER worker (app.py:180-188) and, with a default repo_root, reads the ambient REBAR_TRACKER_DIR persistent worktree (docker-compose.yml:120-124: REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always, no pull configured).

classify_plan_review_attestation -> _plan_review_anchor -> resolve_event_commit runs `git log --full-history` over the tickets-branch to find the attestation's introducing commit (authorship.py:131-160); on any failure it returns None -> the classifier degrades to an infra 'error' verdict (bugfix_size_gate.py:289-291), which the plan explicitly refuses ('an infra verdict ... must NOT auto-accept via this new arm').

_reads.show_ticket applies only a best-effort, throttled (<=1/min) fetch (_reads.py:10-16), so a just-run review can throttle the fetch out and leave the receiver store lagging the freshly-pushed attestation — classifying it as unsigned/absent (bugfix_size_gate.py:227-229).
The premise is that the contributor JUST earned + pushed the attestation to origin/tickets before commenting recheck-review — precisely the read the receiver store must already reflect.
findings.finding: The plan calls the gate's classify_plan_review_attestation(ticket_id) in the recheck-review path but never specifies WHICH ticket store it reads, so the just-earned attestation may not be resolvable there — silently refusing the exact scenario the arm targets.
findings.location: Design — step 4 ('Re-classify with ... classify_plan_review_attestation(ticket_id)') and 'What must still refuse' (the infra arm)
scenarios: Contributor runs `rebar review-plan <id>` (PASS, signed), pushes the attestation to origin/tickets, immediately comments recheck-review; the receiver's store has not yet fetched it -> classifier returns unsigned/absent -> wrongly REFUSED.

The receiver store can read the attestation record but cannot resolve its storage-anchor commit (history depth / unfetched commit) -> _plan_review_anchor None -> infra 'error' verdict -> REFUSED via the infra arm, even though the attestation is genuinely accepted.
findings.suggested_fix: Before classifying, run a non-throttled `git fetch origin tickets` + reconverge on the receiver store (or materialize a fresh tickets snapshot) and pass its repo_root into classify_plan_review_attestation, mirroring the per-review gate's origin/tickets pin; add an AC/test that an attestation pushed AFTER the finding was cast is seen and accepted, and that a receiver store lacking the anchor is treated as infra (refused with the observed verdict named), not falsely accepted.
